scenario_description:
Objective: Keep the afternoon community demo from creating avoidable clay-dust exposure after fresh sanding in the detached studio.
Emerging Need: The visit is initially routine, then workbench dust plus unexpected fan operation make the enclosed studio a developing air-quality risk.
Decision Context: Stored studio-dust guidance and contact records distinguish ordinary cleanup from the symptom pattern needing a time-limited HEPA wet-cleaning route.
Consequence: If the route window closes, no exposure or illness has occurred yet, but the demo remains scheduled before the studio can get the intended dust-control assurance. The closed route concerns specialist cleaning before the planned 15:00 demonstration; postponing the firing or demonstration and keeping the studio closed can remain useful afterward.

parameter.title: Community glaze demo visit
parameter.description: Small group visit to see underglaze tests and trimming-to-firing setup in the detached studio.

parameter.content: I finished dry-fitting and sanding the porcelain test cups on the south workbench. I bagged the scraps and left only a light white powder on the bench edge; the box fan stayed unplugged while I was there.

parameter.subject: Detached studio particulate spike
parameter.body: The detached studio monitor recorded PM10 above its workshop threshold from 09:44 to 09:58. The ceiling-fan smart plug was active during the same interval, and the south-bench zone still shows elevated particulates compared with the courtyard sensor.

parameter.subject: Sunday route board closed
parameter.body: Mesa Studio Dust Care has closed the Sunday same-day route board. Unbooked clay-studio HEPA vacuum and wet-wipe cleanouts received after 12:30 Mountain will be placed on Monday callback unless a prior route slot was already confirmed.
